hypothesis: If Darwin is right that new species 'have appeared very slowly, one after another, both on the land and in the waters', then in the Paleobiology Database's record of Cenozoic animal genera (Danian to Piacenzian, 66 to 2.58 Ma, the Tertiary of Darwin's day), the first appearances of new genera, measured as a per-capita rate per million years, are spread over the stages rather than packed into a few simultaneous pulses, separately for marine and for terrestrial environments: at most one stage per environment has an origination rate that is an outlier above the other stages, and new genera first appear in at least 80 % of the usable stages.
pass_criterion: Pre-registered (claim supported, as a raw-count, stage-resolution result). Primary analysis: PBDB occs/diversity, base_name Metazoa, count genera, time_reso stage, envtype marine and envtype terr (two queries), min_ma 2.58, max_ma 66 (the 17 stages Danian to Piacenzian). Per stage i and environment e: F_i = X_Ft + X_FL (genera whose first occurrence lies in the stage), D_i = X_bt + X_bL + X_Ft + X_FL (genera present in the stage including range-through), dt_i = max_ma - min_ma, o_i = F_i / (D_i * dt_i) (per-capita origination per Myr). A stage is USABLE for environment e if D_i >= 50. A stage is a PULSE if its modified z-score z_i = 0.6745 * (o_i - median(o)) / MAD(o) over the usable stages of that environment is > 3.5 (Iglewicz-Hoaglin outlier convention; if MAD = 0 no stage is a pulse and the case is reported). A stage is POPULATED if F_i >= 5. PASS requires, for BOTH environments: (a) at least 12 usable stages; (b) at most 1 pulse stage; (c) at least 80 % of usable stages are populated.
fail_criterion: Pre-registered (claim refuted, as a raw-count, stage-resolution result). FAIL if, in at least one environment that has at least 12 usable stages, EITHER (a) at least 3 usable stages are pulses (z_i > 3.5), OR (b) fewer than 60 % of usable stages are populated (F_i >= 5), i.e. new genera appear in only a minority of intervals. MIXED: any outcome that is neither pass nor fail, for example exactly 2 pulse stages, or 60 % to <80 % populated stages, or the terrestrial record has fewer than 12 usable stages while the marine record has 12 or more and does not fail (then the land half is untested and the verdict is 'mixed' with the reason recorded). INCONCLUSIVE (reason 'underpowered' or 'data-unavailable'): the marine record has fewer than 12 usable stages; or either query returns fewer than 17 rows in the window or lacks any of the columns X_Ft, X_FL, X_bL, X_bt, n_occs; or the endpoint is unreachable at run time; or the environment filter is rejected for terrestrial and no alternative documented code is available (then only the marine half is reported and the verdict cannot be better than mixed). The thresholds (D >= 50, F >= 5, z > 3.5, at most 1 / at least 3 pulses, 80 % / 60 %, 12 usable stages) are fixed now and are not to be tuned after the data are seen; any deviation must be recorded in a 'deviations' field.

datasets.role: per-stage counts of fossil animal genera by first and last appearance relative to the stage boundaries, separately for marine and terrestrial collections, from which the per-capita origination rate per stage is computed
datasets.scout_record: test-data/dataset-scouting/darwin-origin/darwin1859-ch10-01/datasets.json (status data-ready; the scout recorded that envtype=terr was rejected as 'bad value' on the occs/list operation and that a marine-filtered count query timed out; the diversity operation with envtype was not checked by the scout)
datasets.column_definitions_note: Column names X_Ft, X_bL, X_FL, X_bt follow Foote 2000, Paleobiology 26(4), as cited in the service documentation; X_Ft = taxa with first occurrence in the interval that cross the top boundary, X_FL = taxa found only in the interval, X_bL = taxa that cross the bottom boundary and have their last occurrence in the interval, X_bt = taxa crossing both boundaries. The run confirms these against diversity_doc.html before analysis.

test_contract.expected_observation: In both marine and terrestrial animal records, the per-capita rate at which new genera first appear per million years is roughly even across the Cenozoic stages: no more than one stage stands out as an origination pulse, and new genera appear in almost every stage (at least 80 % of usable stages).
test_contract.disconfirming_observation: In either environment, three or more stages stand out as pulses of origination (modified z > 3.5 above the other stages), or new genera (at least 5) appear in fewer than 60 % of the usable stages: that is, first appearances come in a few simultaneous batches or are absent for most of the record, rather than appearing one after another.
test_contract.admissible_datasets: Open, licensed compilations of dated fossil occurrences or ranges of animals, with per-interval counts of first appearances and range-through taxa at stage resolution (about 10 Myr or finer), separable into marine and terrestrial environments, compiled independently of Darwin's text, covering at least 12 consecutive Cenozoic stages. Counts must be of taxa (genera or species), not of occurrences or collections. Raw (not sampling-standardized) counts are admissible for this test, which must be labelled as such; sampling-standardized and species-level versions are separate tests.
test_contract.inference_method: Per environment, per stage: o_i = (X_Ft + X_FL) / [(X_bt + X_bL + X_Ft + X_FL) * dt_i]. Over the usable stages (D_i >= 50) compute the median and the median absolute deviation (MAD, unscaled) of o_i, the modified z-score z_i = 0.6745 * (o_i - median) / MAD, the number of pulse stages (z_i > 3.5) and the share of usable stages with at least 5 new genera. Apply the numeric thresholds in pass_criterion and fail_criterion; there is no p-value and no resampling. Descriptive only, not used for the verdict: see secondary_analyses_descriptive.

secondary_analyses_descriptive: The same statistics with the Danian and Selandian removed (the post-Cretaceous-Paleogene recovery, which is a known legitimate radiation that Darwin could not have known), reported beside the primary result and not used for the verdict.

Spearman correlation across usable stages between o_i and ln(n_occs) in each environment (a sampling-effort check: a pulse that coincides with a spike in occurrences is suspect), and between o_i and ln(dt_i) (stage length artefact).
The pulse count when the threshold is 3.0 and 4.0 instead of 3.5, and when dt_i is not divided out (share of new genera per stage), to show how much the verdict depends on the convention.
Per stage F_i, D_i, o_i and z_i in a table, the identity of any pulse stage, and the number of usable stages per environment.
The same statistic for the Cenozoic with no environment filter (Metazoa, all collections), for comparison with the pre-registered environment-specific queries.
interpretation: Darwin's sentence asserts a pattern of succession: new species arise 'very slowly, one after another' on the land and in the waters, and not 'in simultaneous batches'. It is mapped here to: 'new species' = first appearances of genera in the Paleobiology Database (modern reinterpretation: genus level, because fossil species counts are too incomplete); 'very slowly' and 'one after another' = first appearances are spread over most stages and no single stage carries a disproportionate share, measured as an origination rate per capita per Myr whose stage-to-stage distribution contains at most one outlier; 'simultaneous batches' = stages whose per-capita origination rate is an outlier (modified z > 3.5) among the other stages of the same environment; 'on land and in the waters' = collections with PBDB environment code terr and marine respectively; 'especially Tertiary' (the claim's scope) = the stages from the Danian to the Piacenzian. The numeric cut-offs (z of 3.5, 1 and 3 pulses, 80 % and 60 % populated stages, at least 50 genera and 5 new genera per stage, at least 12 usable stages) are conventional round values chosen from the claim's wording before any count was viewed, not derived from data, and are a modern operationalization, not Darwin's. The temporal grain is the geological stage (roughly 2 to 8 Myr in the Cenozoic): a pulse shorter than a stage cannot be separated from a gradual appearance, and a stage-level outlier says only that a stage has a high rate, not that its genera appeared simultaneously within it. Conversely the test cannot show that appearances were 'one after another' within a stage. What this test does not cover: species (not genera); the 'very slowly' rate in absolute terms (no absolute rate benchmark is set); any period before the Cenozoic; the cause of any pulse (real radiation, a sampling spike, a hiatus, or a taxonomic artefact such as a monographed fauna); sampling-standardized origination (a separate and larger test); organisms that fossilize poorly; and the distinction between a true origination and the first appearance of a genus in the record. The test is distinct from the registrations for claims darwin1859-ch10-10 (balance of origination and extinction) and darwin1859-ch10-03 (land versus sea turnover): it concerns the temporal distribution of origination only, within each environment. A pass supports only the weak reading that, in the raw stage-level PBDB record, origination is not concentrated in a few outlier stages; a fail refutes only that the raw record shows even succession, not that new species arose in synchronous batches.
caveats: Before this registration was written the following were inspected: the claim text and the scout's record (which gives dataset-level counts and field names, no per-stage values); the three assessors' operationalizations; the two sibling pre-registrations in this batch (darwin1859-ch10-10 and darwin1859-ch04-26), which state that the occs/diversity CSV for Metazoa genera by stage has 22 rows over 0 to 66 Ma and the same column names, and that the diversity operation accepts envtype=marine (21 rows); and the occs/diversity documentation page (HTTP 200, 54,244 bytes), which describes envtype as accepting codes such as 'terr' and 'marine' and time_reso=stage. The data themselves were not opened: no value in X_Ft, X_FL, X_bL, X_bt, sampled_in_bin, implied_in_bin or n_occs was viewed and no rate or statistic was computed. Request status is updated in the 'requests_made' field below.

The scout recorded that envtype=terr was rejected as 'bad value' on the occs/list operation, and that a marine-filtered count query timed out. Whether occs/diversity accepts envtype=terr is therefore not established by this registration; the inconclusive rule covers the case that it does not. If the endpoint rejects 'terr', the documented alternative is a list of terrestrial environment codes from the documentation; that substitution would be recorded in 'deviations' and cannot change any numeric threshold.

Prior knowledge of the likely outcome: the author expects from the palaeontological literature (cited from memory, not re-verified in this session) that the Danian, and possibly the Ypresian-Lutetian interval (including the Eocene mammal and the early Eocene thermal maximum records), may stand out in origination, and that the terrestrial PBDB record is far thinner than the marine one, so that fewer than 12 terrestrial stages may reach D >= 50 genera; a 'mixed' or 'fail' result is plausible, and a stage-level pulse in a thin terrestrial record may reflect sampling. The thresholds were fixed from the claim's wording and conventional values, not from any expected value or any count.

Raw counts, no sampling standardization. Occurrence-poor stages can produce spurious outlier rates and short stages (about 2 Myr) produce noisy rates per Myr. The usable-stage filter (D >= 50) is a partial guard only.

Boundary-crosser counts treat range-through taxa as present in intermediate stages (range-through assumption); the pull of the Recent affects the final stages mainly for extinction, and edge effects at the Danian (the lower bound is the Cretaceous-Paleogene boundary) are possible. The Quaternary is excluded (max 2.58 Ma).

The modified z-score uses the median and MAD of at most 17 stages per environment, so it is itself noisy; adjacent stages share boundary counts and are not independent, and no inference or significance test is attached. The outcome is a descriptive rule with fixed thresholds, not a hypothesis test.
PBDB is a live database and changes as occurrences are added; the run records the access time and the SHA-256 of each response, and a re-run on a later snapshot is a replicate, not new evidence.
Metazoa with an environment filter includes only collections with an environment code; collections without a code are absent from both environment-specific queries.
If completed, the data kind is 'biological' (fossil occurrence counts).
